ops.title: cc-notes in a monorepo: status is spawn-bound, relevant is shallow-walk-bound — and four plausible causes that are wrong
ops.body:
Measured 2026-07-29 on /Users/yasyf/Code/monorepo (11.5 GB pack, 5,913 local refs,
14,704 refs on the remote, 127 refs/cc-notes/*, SHALLOW clone). Three adversarial
verification passes; the refuted hypotheses below are as load-bearing as the confirmed ones.

CONFIRMED — go-git ignores .git/shallow in the read path.
commit_walker.go:43-77 follows ParentHashes unconditionally; .Shallow() is read only by
fetch/push/Merge/Pull. Commit.IsAncestor (merge_base.go:46-59) early-terminates on TRUE
but exhausts the whole reachable history on FALSE. Here: 319 commits shallow, 13,375 past
the graft = 13,694 walked, a 42.9x overshoot over native git.
This dominates `relevant` (12.1s wall / 6.5s CPU; IsAncestor is 76 of 78 resolvable
Client.Relevant frames, via branchAnchorMerged over 16 branch anchors — 167 local
branches, only 14 merged, so nearly every check returns false).

CONFIRMED — `status` is spawn-bound, NOT walk-bound. This was the surprise.
19.8s wall against 2.17s CPU; ~9,593 of ~10,500 sampled ticks blocked in
__wait4_nocancel. It spawns 40-64 `git rev-parse --verify --quiet <HEAD>:<path>` children,
one per path/dir anchor, from notes/document.go driftedOf -> liveAnchorOID ->
gitcmd.PathOID. Anchor census over 82 entities / 187 anchors: path=123, dir=43, branch=16,
commit=5. Notes+docs hold 139 path/dir anchors but only 4 commit anchors, and driftedOf's
`case model.AnchorBranch:` is an empty no-op — so status makes at most 4 ancestry calls,
bounded above by its 0.98s user CPU (<=5% of wall).

CONFIRMED — gitobj.Open passes zero filesystem.Options, so the pack reopens per read.
KeepDescriptors=false and MaxOpenDescriptors=0 mean getFromPackfile (object.go:482) closes
the pack on every object read; the object cache is consulted only inside decodeObjectAt,
AFTER the open. ~219k opens of an 11.5 GB pack. Observable signature: sys CPU (3.9s)
exceeds user CPU (2.6s).

MACHINE CONTEXT — SentinelOne EDR makes every process spawn cost 290ms-1.2s.
`/bin/echo` is as slow as `git`. Any per-item subprocess design is pathological here.
Batching works: one `git cat-file --batch-check` answered 20 lookups in 1.66s vs 18.81s
for 20 spawns.

REFUTED — do not re-derive these:
- "retry() -> Reindex() on the 11 GB pack blocks." Every commit past the boundary is
  PRESENT, so staleIndex() never returns true and Reindex() never fires (zero such frames
  in a 12s sample). And Reindex() is `s.index = nil`; the lazy reload re-decodes 10.1 MB
  of .idx, never the pack.
- "The global Repo.mu negates the errgroup fan-outs." The profiled hot path has NO
  errgroup — ReviewNotes/ReviewDocs are serial for loops. Worth <=4% anywhere, and go-git's
  storage/filesystem has zero synchronization primitives, so mu is NOT safely removable.
  Fixing the descriptor ring and memoizing the root tree both WIDEN what mu must protect.
- "The default object LRU is small." It is 96 MiB (plumbing/cache/common.go:14).
- "ListPrefix's all-refs scan is a cost center." ~50ms delta between a 555-ref and a
  5,913-ref repo.

SYNC IS NOT THE CULPRIT. All three sync-engine IsAncestor sites (internal/sync/sync.go
:272, :359, :366) compare two tips of the SAME entity ref; chains are depth 2 (mode and
median, max 35; 442 commits across all 127 refs), so one check reads ~2 commit objects.
internal/sync/reconcile.go:126 is in the exported Reconcile behind `cc-notes reconcile`,
which Sync never calls. Fetch/push refspecs are correctly namespace-scoped. Sync wall time
in a monorepo remains UNMEASURED — the repo has zero benchmarks and sync has no --verbose,
so any future sync investigation must start by adding timing.
